subproblems.title: Cut-off quadratic moments over n-planes, with a constant depending only on n
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, and for every P ∈ ℕ let Hⁿ = μHE[n] be the normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). There is a single constant c > 0 depending only on n — the same c for every ambient dimension P, every subspace Q and every vector u — such that for every P ∈ ℕ, every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with dim Q = n and every u ∈ ℝ^P, ∫_Q max(1 − |y|², 0)·⟨u, y⟩² dHⁿ(y) = c·|p_Q u|². Here ∫_Q means integration against Hⁿ⌞Q (Hⁿ on ℝ^P restricted to Q) and p_Q = Q.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → ∀ u : Euclid P, ∫ y in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), max (1 - ‖y‖ ^ 2) 0 * inner ℝ u y ^ 2 ∂μHE[n] = c * ‖Q.starProjection u‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted DAG theorem with identical frozen Lean type (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.tangent_projection_aemeasurable-a1.plane_quadratic_moment-a1, status accepted, candidate 2b2d626519e4, isolated comparator passed). Its content is step 2(a) of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent; the complete accepted proof follows.
Source: step 4 of the parent-supplied proof of imrep_univ_tangent_starProjection_aemeasurable, which sets c_n := ∫_{ℝⁿ} χ(|z|²) z_1² dz with χ(t) = max(1 − t, 0). That proof establishes the measurability of the approximate tangent planes of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86), which Simon uses implicitly. Simon prints no proof of this computation, so the parent's argument is reproduced here with all details. The constant is defined on ℝⁿ alone, before any ambient dimension is chosen; this is why one constant serves every P.

Notation. Fix n ≥ 1. Hⁿ := μHE[n], on ℝ^P for each P and on ℝⁿ. For a set A, ∫_A g dHⁿ means ∫ g d(Hⁿ⌞A). E_n := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume). Since n ≥ 1, the index i₀ := 0 ∈ Fin n exists. For i, j ∈ Fin n and z ∈ E_n put h_{ij}(z) := max(1 − |z|², 0)·z_i·z_j, and define c := ∫_{E_n} h_{i₀i₀} dLⁿ. Only n enters this definition: c does not depend on any ambient dimension P, subspace Q or vector u.

1. Integrability. Each h_{ij} is continuous: it is built from the norm, the coordinate maps, max and products. If |z| > 1 then 1 − |z|² < 0, so max(1 − |z|², 0) = 0 and h_{ij}(z) = 0. Hence h_{ij} has support in the closed unit ball, which is compact. Lⁿ is finite on compact sets, so a continuous compactly supported function is Lⁿ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).

2. Off-diagonal moments vanish. Let i ≠ j. Let S : E_n → E_n negate the i-th coordinate: (Sz)_k = −z_k for k = i and (Sz)_k = z_k for k ≠ i. In Lean this is LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrRight 2 with −id in slot i and id elsewhere.
- S is a linear isometry equivalence, so |Sz| = |z|.
- S preserves Lⁿ (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving).
- Being a homeomorphism, S is a measurable embedding.
Since (Sz)_i = −z_i and (Sz)_j = z_j, we get h_{ij}(Sz) = −h_{ij}(z) for all z. By change of variables for measure-preserving embeddings (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp), ∫ h_{ij} dLⁿ = ∫ h_{ij}(Sz) dLⁿ(z) = −∫ h_{ij} dLⁿ. Hence ∫ h_{ij} dLⁿ = 0.

3. Diagonal moments are all equal to c. Fix i. Let T : E_n → E_n permute the coordinates by the transposition σ = swap(i₀, i), so (Tz)_k = z_{σ(k)}. In Lean this is LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℝ ℝ (Equiv.swap i₀ i).
- T is a linear isometry equivalence, so |Tz| = |z|, and T preserves Lⁿ.
- (Tz)_i = z_{σ(i)} = z_{i₀}.
Hence h_{ii}(Tz) = max(1 − |z|², 0)·z_{i₀}² = h_{i₀i₀}(z). By change of variables, ∫ h_{ii} dLⁿ = ∫ h_{ii}(Tz) dLⁿ(z) = ∫ h_{i₀i₀} dLⁿ = c.

4. c > 0. The function h_{i₀i₀} = max(1 − |z|², 0)·z_{i₀}² is ≥ 0 everywhere and is continuous with compact support (step 1). At z* := (1/2)e_{i₀} we have |z*|² = 1/4, so h_{i₀i₀}(z*) = (3/4)(1/4) = 3/16 ≠ 0. Lⁿ is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on compacts. So the integral of a nonnegative, continuous, compactly supported function that is nonzero at some point is positive (Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero). Thus c > 0. The constant c is now fixed; everything below holds with this same c.

5. Parametrizing Q. Now let P ∈ ℕ be arbitrary, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim Q = n, and let u ∈ ℝ^P. (If n > P there is no such Q, and nothing has to be proved.) Choose an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_n of Q indexed by Fin n, for example stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q reindexed along finrank Q = n. Let ι : E_n → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_i z_i τ_i. This is the inclusion Q → ℝ^P composed with the inverse of the basis' coordinate isometry. By orthonormality, ι is a linear isometry (|ι z| = |z|). Its range is exactly Q: every q ∈ Q equals ι of its coordinate vector, and every Σ z_i τ_i lies in Q.

6. Push-forward of Hausdorff measure.
- Because ι is an isometry, the push-forward of Hⁿ on E_n under ι equals Hⁿ⌞(range ι) = Hⁿ⌞Q (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
- Hⁿ on E_n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is Lⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
- An isometry defined on a complete space is a closed embedding, hence a measurable embedding.
Therefore, writing F(y) := max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩², we get ∫_Q F dHⁿ = ∫ F d(ι_#Lⁿ) = ∫_{E_n} F(ι z) dLⁿ(z) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).

7. Expanding the integrand. Let a_i := ⟨u, τ_i⟩. Then |ι z| = |z| and ⟨u, ι z⟩ = Σ_i z_i a_i. So for every z ∈ E_n, F(ι z) = max(1 − |z|², 0)(Σ_i a_i z_i)² = Σ_i Σ_j a_i a_j h_{ij}(z).

8. Integrating. The finitely many functions a_i a_j h_{ij} are all integrable (step 1), so the integral is additive and homogeneous: ∫_{E_n} F(ι z) dLⁿ = Σ_i Σ_j a_i a_j ∫ h_{ij} dLⁿ. For fixed i, steps 2 and 3 show that only the term j = i survives, and it equals a_i²·c. Hence ∫_Q F dHⁿ = c·Σ_i a_i².

9. Identifying Σ_i a_i². The orthogonal projection onto Q is p_Q v = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, v⟩τ_i (expansion in an orthonormal basis of Q; OrthonormalBasis.starProjection_eq_sum_rankOne). p_Q is self-adjoint (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right) and idempotent (p_Q u ∈ Q is fixed by p_Q). Therefore |p_Q u|² = ⟨p_Q u, p_Q u⟩ = ⟨u, p_Q(p_Q u)⟩ = ⟨u, p_Q u⟩ = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, u⟩⟨u, τ_i⟩ = Σ_i a_i².

10. Conclusion. By steps 6–9, ∫_Q max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩² dHⁿ(y) = c|p_Q u|². The constant c > 0 was fixed in the Notation paragraph and step 4, before P, Q and u were chosen in step 5. So one and the same c works for every P ∈ ℕ, every n-dimensional subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P and every u ∈ ℝ^P, which is exactly the claim: ∃ c > 0, ∀ P, ∀ Q with dim Q = n, ∀ u, ∫_Q max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩² dHⁿ(y) = c|p_Q u|². ∎
proof_key_steps: Define c := ∫_{ℝⁿ} max(1−|z|²,0) z_{i₀}² dLⁿ(z), which involves only n; every h_{ij}(z) = max(1−|z|²,0)z_iz_j is continuous with support in the closed unit ball, hence integrable.
Coordinate reflections (linear isometries preserving Lebesgue measure) give ∫h_{ij} = 0 for i ≠ j; coordinate swaps give ∫h_{ii} = c.
c > 0: the integrand is continuous, ≥ 0, compactly supported and equals 3/16 at e_{i₀}/2.
For arbitrary P, Q ⊆ ℝ^P with dim Q = n and u ∈ ℝ^P: an orthonormal basis τ of Q gives a linear isometry ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P onto Q with ι_#Lⁿ = Hⁿ⌞Q, so ∫_Q f_u dHⁿ = ∫ f_u∘ι dLⁿ.
f_u∘ι = Σ_{i,j} a_ia_j h_{ij} with a_i = ⟨u,τ_i⟩, so the integral is cΣa_i² = c|p_Q u|², with the same c (fixed before P, Q, u) for all P, Q, u.

subproblems.title: Blow-up integrals over a locally Hⁿ-finite set are continuous in the centre
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be any set such that Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support, and let r > 0. Put η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT Chapter03.blowUpMap x r). Then x ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ, the integral of f against Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M), is a continuous function on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μHE[n] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → Continuous (fun x : Euclid P => ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' M, f y ∂μHE[n])
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted DAG theorem with identical frozen Lean type (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.tangent_projection_aemeasurable-a1.blowup_integral_continuous-a1, status accepted, candidate fad2341d37df, isolated comparator passed). Its content is step 2(b) of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent; the complete accepted proof follows.
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of imrep_univ_tangent_starProjection_aemeasurable. The integral is the one in Simon's Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86; SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt), where M is likewise assumed to have Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K. Simon prints no proof, so the parent's argument is given with all details. It uses neither measurability of M nor any property of M beyond the local-finiteness hypothesis.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. For a set A, ∫_A g dHⁿ := ∫ g d(Hⁿ⌞A). η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x r), and ν := Hⁿ⌞M.

1. Scaling of Hⁿ under η_{x,r}. Fix x ∈ ℝ^P. Claim: Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(S) for every set S ⊆ ℝ^P, measurable or not. Indeed η_{x,r}(S) = h(τ(S)), where τ(y) := y − x and h(z) := r⁻¹z.
- τ is an isometry of ℝ^P, and isometries preserve Hⁿ of every set (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- h is the homothety with centre 0 and ratio r⁻¹ ≠ 0, so Hⁿ(h(S')) = |r⁻¹|ⁿHⁿ(S') for every S' (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image).
As r > 0, |r⁻¹|ⁿ = r⁻ⁿ.

2. Push-forward identity. b := η_{x,r} is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse b⁻¹(z) = x + rz. Let ν_x := Hⁿ⌞b(M). Claim: (b⁻¹)_#ν_x = r⁻ⁿν. Let A be a Borel set. Then (b⁻¹)⁻¹(A) = b(A), which is Borel, and
(b⁻¹)_#ν_x(A) = ν_x(b(A)) = Hⁿ(b(A) ∩ b(M)) = Hⁿ(b(A ∩ M)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(A ∩ M) = r⁻ⁿν(A).
The third equality uses that b is injective, and the fourth uses step 1. Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal.

3. Change of variables. b⁻¹ is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding. Applying MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map to the function f∘b:
∫ f dν_x = ∫ (f∘b)(b⁻¹z) dν_x(z) = ∫ f∘b d((b⁻¹)_#ν_x) = ∫ f∘b d(r⁻ⁿν) = r⁻ⁿ∫ f(r⁻¹(y − x)) dν(y).
Hence, for every x, Φ(x) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = r⁻ⁿΨ(x), where Ψ(x) := ∫_M f(r⁻¹(y − x)) dHⁿ(y).

4. Bounds for f. Since f is continuous with compact support, there is C ≥ 0 with |f(z)| ≤ C for all z, and there is R ≥ 0 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R).

5. Local domination. Fix x₀ ∈ ℝ^P and let B := closedBall(x₀, 1 + rR), a compact set. Let x ∈ ball(x₀, 1) and let y ∈ ℝ^P with y ∉ B. Suppose f(r⁻¹(y − x)) ≠ 0. Then r⁻¹(y − x) ∈ tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R), so |y − x| ≤ rR and |y − x₀| ≤ |y − x| + |x − x₀| < rR + 1. That means y ∈ B, a contradiction. Hence |f(r⁻¹(y − x))| ≤ C·1_B(y) for all y ∈ ℝ^P and all x ∈ ball(x₀, 1).

6. The dominating function is integrable. B is Borel, so ν(B) = Hⁿ(B ∩ M) = Hⁿ(M ∩ B). This is finite by the hypothesis applied to the compact set B. Therefore C·1_B is ν-integrable.

7. Measurability and pointwise continuity. For each x, the map y ↦ f(r⁻¹(y − x)) is continuous, hence (strongly) measurable. For each y, the map x ↦ f(r⁻¹(y − x)) is continuous.

8. Dominated convergence. Apply the dominated convergence theorem for parameter-dependent integrals (continuousAt_of_dominated) with the bound of step 5, which is valid on the neighbourhood ball(x₀, 1) of x₀, the integrable bound of step 6 and the continuity of step 7. It shows that Ψ is continuous at x₀. Since x₀ is arbitrary, Ψ is continuous on ℝ^P. By step 3, so is Φ = r⁻ⁿΨ; that is, x ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ is continuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(S) for every set S (the translation is an isometry, followed by a homothety of ratio r⁻¹).
(η_{x,r}⁻¹)_#(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ⌞M, hence ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = r⁻ⁿ∫_M f(r⁻¹(y−x)) dHⁿ(y).
For x ∈ ball(x₀,1) the integrand is bounded by sup|f|·1_{closedBall(x₀,1+rR)}, which is integrable because Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K.

subproblems.title: A field of orthogonal projections is a.e.-measurable when its quadratic forms are
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and let K be a map from ℝ^P to linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Let p_x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) be the orthogonal projection onto K(x), i.e. (K x).starProjection. Suppose that for every u ∈ ℝ^P the real function x ↦ |p_x u|² is μ-a.e. measurable. Then x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. measurable for the Borel σ-algebra of L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) with the operator-norm topology.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (K : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ u : Euclid P, AEMeasurable (fun x => ‖(K x).starProjection u‖ ^ 2) μ) → AEMeasurable (fun x => (K x).starProjection) μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted DAG theorem with identical frozen Lean type (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.tangent_projection_aemeasurable-a1.projection_field_aemeasurable-a1, status accepted, candidate 3c953dc51e92, isolated comparator passed). Its content is step 2(d) of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent; the complete accepted proof follows.
Source: steps 7–8 of the parent-supplied proof of imrep_univ_tangent_starProjection_aemeasurable. There, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the approximate tangent plane. The argument uses only that each p_x is an orthogonal projection, so it is given here for an arbitrary field of subspaces and an arbitrary measure.

Notation. ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product of ℝ^P, and p_x := (K x).starProjection. L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) carries the operator-norm topology and its Borel σ-algebra (ContinuousLinearMap.instMeasurableSpace = borel).

1. Self-adjointness and idempotence. For every x and all v, w ∈ ℝ^P, ⟨p_x v, w⟩ = ⟨v, p_x w⟩ (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right). Also p_x(p_x w) = p_x w, because p_x w ∈ K(x) and p_x fixes K(x) pointwise (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff).

2. Polarization. Let u, w ∈ ℝ^P. By step 1, ⟨p_x u, w⟩ = ⟨u, p_x w⟩ = ⟨u, p_x(p_x w)⟩ = ⟨p_x u, p_x w⟩. For real vectors a, b we have |a ± b|² = |a|² ± 2⟨a, b⟩ + |b|², so ⟨a, b⟩ = (|a + b|² − |a − b|²)/4. Take a = p_x u and b = p_x w, and use linearity: p_x u ± p_x w = p_x(u ± w). This gives, for every x, ⟨p_x u, w⟩ = (|p_x(u + w)|² − |p_x(u − w)|²)/4.

3. Matrix coefficients are a.e.-measurable. By hypothesis, x ↦ |p_x(u + w)|² and x ↦ |p_x(u − w)|² are μ-AEMeasurable. Differences and constant multiples of AEMeasurable real functions are AEMeasurable. So by step 2, x ↦ ⟨p_x u, w⟩ is μ-AEMeasurable for all u, w ∈ ℝ^P.

4. Basis expansion. Let e_1, …, e_P be the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
- For (a, b) ∈ Fin P × Fin P let L_{ab} ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), L_{ab}(v) := ⟨e_a, v⟩e_b.
- Let Λ : ℝ^{Fin P × Fin P} → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), Λ(m) := Σ_{a,b} m_{ab}L_{ab}.
- Put g(x) := (⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩)_{(a,b)} ∈ ℝ^{Fin P × Fin P}.
Fix x and v. Since v = Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩e_a, we have p_x v = Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩ p_x e_a. Also p_x e_a = Σ_b ⟨e_b, p_x e_a⟩e_b = Σ_b ⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩e_b. Hence p_x v = Σ_{a,b} ⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩⟨e_a, v⟩e_b = Λ(g(x))(v). So p_x = Λ(g(x)) for every x.

5. Conclusion. Λ is a finite sum of the continuous linear maps m ↦ m_{ab}L_{ab} (a coordinate projection times a fixed operator). So Λ is continuous linear, hence Borel measurable. g is μ-AEMeasurable as a map into the finite product ℝ^{Fin P × Fin P}, because each of its coordinates is (step 3; AEMeasurable.of_eval). A measurable map composed with a μ-AEMeasurable map is μ-AEMeasurable (Measurable.comp_aemeasurable). Therefore x ↦ p_x = Λ(g(x)) is μ-AEMeasurable. If P = 0, all spaces are trivial and the same argument applies with empty sums. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, so ⟨p_x u, w⟩ = ⟨p_x u, p_x w⟩ = (|p_x(u+w)|² − |p_x(u−w)|²)/4.
Hence every matrix coefficient x ↦ ⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩ is μ-a.e. measurable.
p_x = Λ((⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩)_{a,b}), where Λ(m) = Σ m_{ab}⟨e_a,·⟩e_b is a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional coefficient space.
A continuous map composed with an a.e.-measurable map into ℝ^{P×P} is a.e.-measurable.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes are unchanged by H^n-null modifications of the set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and A, B ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(A ∖ B) = 0 and H^n(B ∖ A) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n]. Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P: Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q: finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), with η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x)) if and only if Q is an approximate tangent space of B at x.

Its content is step 5 of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent; the complete accepted proof follows.
Source: step 4 of the parent proof of representation independence of θH^n⌞M (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3)): blow-ups of H^n-a.e. equal sets coincide up to H^n-null sets, so the limits in Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (approximate tangent space) agree.

Notation: H^n = μHE[n]; for r ∈ ℝ, b_r := blowUpMap x r, b_r(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) (Simon's η_{x,r}).
1. (Definition.) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), φ_M^f(r) := ∫_{b_r(M)} f dH^n converges to ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0 with r > 0 (along the filter 𝓝[>] 0).
2. (Null sets stay null under b_r, r ≠ 0.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(S) = 0. Then b_r(S) = r^{-1}·(S − x), where S − x is the image of S under the isometry y ↦ y − x. Isometries preserve H^n (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so H^n(S − x) = 0; and H^n(c·S') = |c|^n·H^n(S') for c ≠ 0 (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Hence H^n(b_r(S)) = 0.
3. (The blow-ups agree up to null sets.) For any map b, b(A) ∖ b(B) ⊆ b(A ∖ B): if y = b(a) with a ∈ A and y ∉ b(B), then a ∉ B (Mathlib Set.subset_image_sdiff). Likewise b(B) ∖ b(A) ⊆ b(B ∖ A). By the hypotheses H^n(A ∖ B) = 0 = H^n(B ∖ A) and step 2, for every r ≠ 0 both differences b_r(A) ∖ b_r(B) and b_r(B) ∖ b_r(A) are H^n-null, i.e. b_r(A) and b_r(B) coincide up to an H^n-null set (Mathlib ae_eq_set). Consequently H^n⌞b_r(A) = H^n⌞b_r(B), and φ_A^f(r) = φ_B^f(r) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and every r ≠ 0 (Mathlib setIntegral_congr_set). No integrability is needed: the two set integrals are integrals against the same restricted measure.
4. (The limits agree.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin) and φ_A^f = φ_B^f on it by step 3, so φ_A^f converges to L along 𝓝[>] 0 if and only if φ_B^f does (Filter.Tendsto.congr').
5. The dimension clause finrank Q = n is literally the same on both sides. Combining it with step 4 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, for every x and every Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: For r ≠ 0, η_{x,r} is a translation followed by a dilation, so it maps H^n-null sets to H^n-null sets.
η(A) ∖ η(B) ⊆ η(A ∖ B) and η(B) ∖ η(A) ⊆ η(B ∖ A), so the blow-ups of A and B agree up to H^n-null sets and their integrals coincide for every r > 0.
Functions that agree on (0, ∞) have the same limits along 𝓝[>] 0, and the dimension clause is shared, so the two predicates are equivalent.

subproblems.title: A.e. strong measurability of an approximate-tangent-plane projection field
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be any set (measurability is not assumed) with Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let Q be any map from ℝ^P to the linear subspaces of ℝ^P such that, for Hⁿ⌞M-almost every x, Q(x) is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x): dim Q(x) = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_{Q(x)} f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is blowUpMap x r). Then the field of orthogonal projections x ↦ p_{Q(x)} = (Q x).starProjection ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable for μHE[n].restrict M).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μHE[n] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x)) → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict M)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent (measurability of the tangent-plane field), stated for an arbitrary a.e. approximate-tangent field Q instead of approxTangentPlane n M; the parent applies it with Q := approxTangentPlane n M. Steps 2(a), 2(b) and 2(d) of that proof are the sibling theorems (QM) = exists_plane_cutoff_quadratic_moment_eq, (BC) = continuous_blowUp_image_setIntegral and (PF) = aemeasurable_starProjection_of_aemeasurable_norm_sq, used exactly as stated; step 2(c) is carried out below.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; p_x := (Q x).starProjection; η_{x,r} := blowUpMap x r, η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x); ∫_A g dHⁿ := ∫ g d(Hⁿ⌞A). Let G be the set of x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x); by hypothesis G holds μ-a.e.

1. Case n = 0. For x ∈ G the dimension clause of the definition gives finrank Q(x) = 0, hence Q(x) = ⊥ (Submodule.finrank_eq_zero), and p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the zero subspace, i.e. p_x v = 0 for every v, so p_x = 0. Thus x ↦ p_x agrees μ-a.e. with the constant map 0, which is strongly measurable, and a function μ-a.e. equal to an a.e. strongly measurable function is a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr). This proves the claim for n = 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

2. The plane moments. By (QM) (applicable since n ≥ 1) there is c > 0 such that for every linear subspace Q' ⊆ ℝ^P with finrank Q' = n and every u ∈ ℝ^P: ∫_{Q'} max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩² dHⁿ(y) = c|p_{Q'} u|².

3. The test function. Fix u ∈ ℝ^P and put f_u(y) := max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩². It is continuous (built from the norm, the inner product, max and products). If |y| > 1 then 1 − |y|² < 0, so max(1 − |y|², 0) = 0 and f_u(y) = 0; hence f_u vanishes outside the compact closed unit ball and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro). So f_u defines an element F_u ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) with F_u(y) = f_u(y) for all y.

4. A sequence of radii. Put r_k := 1/(k + 1), k ∈ ℕ. Then r_k > 0 and r_k → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat); since every r_k lies in (0, ∞), r_k → 0 along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff).

5. Measurable approximants. For k ∈ ℕ let Φ_k(x) := ∫_{η_{x,r_k}(M)} f_u dHⁿ. By (BC), applied to M (its hypothesis Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K is exactly ours), to the continuous compactly supported f_u and to r_k > 0, each Φ_k is continuous on ℝ^P, hence Borel measurable, hence μ-a.e. measurable.

6. Pointwise limits. Let x ∈ G. Applying the definition of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x) to the test function F_u gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f_u dHⁿ → ∫_{Q(x)} f_u dHⁿ as r → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0; composing with step 4, Φ_k(x) → ∫_{Q(x)} f_u dHⁿ as k → ∞. The dimension clause gives finrank Q(x) = n, so by step 2 this limit is c|p_x u|². Hence Φ_k(x) → c|p_x u|² for μ-a.e. x.

7. Quadratic forms are a.e. measurable. A μ-a.e. limit of a sequence of μ-a.e. measurable real functions is μ-a.e. measurable (aemeasurable_of_tendsto_metrizable_ae'). By steps 5–6, x ↦ c|p_x u|² is μ-a.e. measurable; multiplying by the constant c⁻¹ (c > 0) shows that x ↦ |p_x u|² = c⁻¹·(c|p_x u|²) is μ-a.e. measurable. This holds for every u ∈ ℝ^P.

8. The projection field. By (PF), applied to the measure μ and the field K := Q, step 7 implies that x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. measurable as a map into L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) with its Borel σ-algebra.

9. Strong measurability. L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence metrizable and second countable, and its σ-algebra is the Borel one; for such targets a.e. measurability implies a.e. strong measurability (AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable). Hence x ↦ (Q x).starProjection is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. ∎

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity from a rectifiable carrier with a.e. integer density and oriented approximate tangent planes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), M ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set that is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel measurable with θ > 0 on M and ∫⁻_M ofReal(θ) dHⁿ < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) strongly measurable, such that Γ(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ζ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every test n-form ω on ℝ^P. Suppose that for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a linear subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4), ζ(x) a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ x) Q) and θ(x) = m for some m ∈ ℕ. Then Γ is an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity Γ): some IMRep R in ℝ^P represents Γ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–7 of the parent proof of cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent (assembly of the IMRep), with the countable n-rectifiability of M (step 3 there, obtained from (RECT)) taken as a hypothesis. Step 5 there is the sibling theorem (NI) = hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_iff_of_null_sdiff, used exactly as stated.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For x ∈ ℝ^P let p(x) be the statement: there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ x) Q, and θ(x) = m for some m ∈ ℕ. By hypothesis p holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.

1. The bad set is null. As M is measurable, the statement that p(x) holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x is equivalent to the statement that x ∈ M → p(x) holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff'), i.e. B := {x : x ∈ M and not p(x)} satisfies Hⁿ(B) = 0 (ae_iff).

2. A Borel carrier of full measure. Let N₀ := toMeasurable(Hⁿ, B): N₀ is measurable, B ⊆ N₀ and Hⁿ(N₀) = Hⁿ(B) = 0 (measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable).
